item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00014","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C24","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.91,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C11 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both letters seek urgent legislation extending benefits to servicemembers from the current Korean-hostilities cohort who are already being separated from service, and both justify immediate congressional action by stressing those individuals’ present needs. C11 even anticipates later legislation providing additional kinds of readjustment help beyond vocational rehabilitation. C24 and C09 share the compact attached-draft-and-prompt-action letter form, but their substantive machinery is unrelated.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Attached is a draft of legislation which would extend certain benefits to persons who shall have served in the Armed Forces on or after June 27, 1950.","parent_excerpt":"However, the benefits of Public Law 16 are not available to men who began their military service after July 25, 1947. This means that most of the men disabled during the current campaign in Korea will not receive the kind of rehabilitation benefits which were extended to the disabled veterans of the last war unless new legislation is enacted.","explanation":"Both propose legislation extending veterans’ benefits to the newly defined Korean-conflict service cohort."},{"child_excerpt":"Unless and until such legislation is enacted, certain individuals already separated from the military service, and whose needs are acute, will be denied medical and hospital care.","parent_excerpt":"Since the armed forces are now beginning to discharge men disabled in the current hostilities, renewal of these benefits has become a matter of urgency... Meanwhile, however, there is no reason for delay in meeting the immediate needs of the disabled servicemen who are now being released by the armed forces.","explanation":"The child closely reproduces C11’s factual and rhetorical justification: servicemembers are already being discharged, their needs are immediate, and existing law does not provide the pertinent benefits."},{"child_excerpt":"I hope the Congress will take favorable action on this legislation at the earliest possible date.","parent_excerpt":"I hope that such legislation will receive favorable action by the Congress before the close of this session.","explanation":"Both close with materially similar requests for favorable and expedited congressional action."}]}
